_note: Original, light-hearted student lore written for the Hostel Pradesh section of this design concept. It is NOT researched food history: no dates, no origin claims, no sources. Every dish is marked 'lore' on the page. Not part of the strict content/ files used by the Astro site.

state.name: Hostel Pradesh
state.intro: Welcome to Hostel Pradesh, the capital of the Bhukkad Republic and its most crowded state. Official language: "bhai, kuch hai kya khane ko?" Main export: Maggi. Main import: care packages from home. Here the kettle is a kitchen and the warden is the final boss.

dishes.name: Kettle Maggi
dishes.summary: Instant noodles cooked straight in the electric kettle. The dish that taught a whole generation to share a kettle, and a secret.
steps: Boil water in the kettle, then switch it off and unplug it.
Break the noodle cake into the hot water, close the lid and wait about four minutes.
Pour most of the water into the sink, add the masala sachet and stir with a clean spoon.
Wash the kettle straight away, or tomorrow's chai will taste of Maggi.

dishes.name: Cheese Maggi
dishes.summary: Plain Maggi, promoted. One cheese slice and a spoon of butter turn a Tuesday into a celebration.
steps: Cook the noodles with the masala sachet and a little less water than usual.
While it is still hot, stir in the butter and tear the cheese slice into it.
Stir until the cheese melts into a glossy sauce, then eat it before anyone smells it.

dishes.name: Maggi Sandwich
dishes.summary: Leftover Maggi packed between two slices of bread. Carbs inside carbs, a hostel classic.
steps: Butter the outside of two bread slices.
Pile cooled Maggi on one slice, close with the other and press down.
Toast on both sides until golden and crisp.

dishes.name: Kettle Khichdi
dishes.summary: Rice and moong dal cooked in a kettle, in rounds. It takes patience, three boils and a very understanding roommate.
steps: Rinse a small handful of rice and moong dal until the water runs clear.
Put them in the kettle with turmeric, salt and plenty of water. Do not fill past the max line.
Boil, switch off, wait ten minutes, then boil again. Repeat until the rice is soft.
Unplug it before opening the lid. Tip into a bowl and add a spoon of ghee if the care package has any.

dishes.name: Hot-Water Poha
dishes.summary: Poha that needs no stove, only hot water and hope. Breakfast for people who woke up six minutes before class.
steps: Rinse the poha quickly, then soak it in hot kettle water for two minutes.
Drain, then stir in salt and a pinch of turmeric.
Top with chopped onion, green chilli, peanuts and a squeeze of lemon.

dishes.name: Kettle Upma
dishes.summary: Rava and hot water, stirred until it stops being soup. A little loose, completely sincere.
steps: Pour hot kettle water over the rava in a steel bowl, a little at a time, stirring all the while.
Cover with a plate and wait five minutes.
Stir in chopped onion, green chilli and salt.

dishes.name: Kettle Chai
dishes.summary: The real hero of every hostel floor. Brewed at midnight, shared with anyone who walks past the door.
steps: Boil water in the kettle with the tea leaves, sugar and a little crushed ginger.
Switch off, add warm milk and let it sit for a minute.
Strain into as many mugs as there are visitors.

dishes.name: Bread-Butter-Chini
dishes.summary: Zero cooking. Bread, butter, a sprinkle of sugar. Maximum comfort.
steps: Butter a slice of bread.
Sprinkle sugar on top.
Fold it, eat it, and feel eight years old again.

dishes.name: Sattu Sharbat
dishes.summary: Roasted gram flour stirred into cold water. The exam-week energy drink that needs no appliance at all.
steps: Stir two spoons of sattu into a glass of cold water until no lumps remain.
Add a squeeze of lemon, a pinch of black salt and roasted cumin.
Drink it fast, before the lumps come back.

dishes.name: Hostel Bhel
dishes.summary: Made from whatever survived the care package: namkeen, puffed rice, one lonely onion and a lemon.
steps: Mix the puffed rice and namkeen on a steel plate.
Add chopped onion, tomato and green chilli.
Finish with lemon and salt, and eat fast so it stays crisp.

dishes.name: Mess-Dal Maggi
dishes.summary: Yesterday's mess dal meets today's Maggi. Nobody planned it, everybody secretly loves it.
steps: Warm the leftover dal with a splash of water.
Add the noodles and cook until soft.
Stir in half the masala sachet, because the dal already has opinions.

dishes.name: Roti Pizza
dishes.summary: A leftover roti with ambitions. Ketchup for sauce, a cheese slice for glory.
steps: Warm the roti on a tawa.
Spread ketchup, add chopped onion and capsicum, and lay the cheese on top.
Cover and heat until the cheese melts.

dishes.name: Jam Toast
dishes.summary: Toast, butter, jam. The breakfast that never lets you down and never asks questions.
steps: Toast the bread.
Spread butter while it is hot, then jam.
Eat standing up, while looking for your other shoe.

dishes.name: Mess Aloo Sandwich
dishes.summary: Last night's dry aloo sabzi, rescued into a sandwich with ketchup. A comeback story.
steps: Mash the leftover aloo sabzi slightly and spread it on a buttered bread slice.
Add ketchup, close with a second slice.
Toast on a tawa until both sides are crisp.
